You are an end-to-end TEST LEARNER for the Catalyte AI Fellowship challenge INSURANCE-01. Kuan (she/her, the program lead) asked for this test to prove that a learner can go from the Classroom post to a graded submission. Work in this repository: ~/Code/ch03-premium-audit-test (a private copy of the starter repo; Entire session capture is already enabled here, so this session is being recorded as the learner's coding session).

## Goal
Do the whole assignment exactly as a learner would and leave a complete, committed repository ready to submit. The PM session (K5) will review it, push it, and Kuan will submit it from a student account. You do NOT push and do NOT submit.

## Learner-only boundary (strict)
Use ONLY what a learner has:
- The Classroom post text below.
- The assignment Google Doc linked in it (read it in full first: it owns scope, deliverables and submission requirements).
- The starter repository README in this repo.
- The Work Sim stakeholder interview at https://work-sim.catalyte.ai/s/ch03-premium-audit and the files/links the stakeholder gives you there.
- The Classroom "Set up your environment" materials, if you need them.
Never read anything else about this challenge: not ~/Documents/challenge-pipeline, not any curriculum repo or worktree, not /private/tmp scratchpads, not ~/Documents/ai-fellowship, not ~/.claude (memory, handoffs, projects), not any interviewee prompt or answer key. If you stumble on such material, stop reading it and mention it in your report.

## The interview
Kuan explicitly chose, for this test only, that you conduct the interview yourself through her logged-in Chrome (use the claude-in-chrome tools; load them in one ToolSearch call; open a new tab). She knows this breaks the learner Interview rule and that the result may be marked as agent-run; do the test anyway.
- Plan for at most 3 conversations. Prepare your questions before each one from what you know so far, and ask completely, like a careful analyst.
- If the page only allows voice and you cannot type, or login is required, stop and report exactly what you saw; do not try to bypass it.
- After each conversation, use the page's own Markdown export and save the original export unchanged as one file per session under interviews/. If there is no export, stop and report.
- Do not trigger browser alert/confirm dialogs. Do not enter any passwords.

## The build
Follow the assignment Doc's deliverables and requirements exactly (Skill, README, per-employer outputs, audit questions, audit report, verification). Run the Skill on all six employers, verify the results, and in this coding session state in your own words whether you accept each employer's own payroll split and what record that rests on (the task asks for this). Commit locally with clear messages as you go. Keep secrets out of the repo.

## Report
When finished (or blocked), write a report to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kj/9f7f1af2-0199-4745-a141-36874ac98a15/scratchpad/ch03-e2e/report.md, in Traditional Chinese, without em or en dashes:
- What you did, final commit hash, `git status`, `entire status` output.
- The interview: how many conversations, export file names, anything that went wrong.
- The assignment Doc's exact submission and access requirements (what must be submitted, whether the grader needs repo access and how), so the PM can complete them.
- Anything in the learner path that was unclear, broken or missing (this is the main value of the test).
Do not write to ~/.claude/topics or ~/.claude/tab-labels.

## Rules you must follow (copied verbatim from the PM's rules)
## 一定要先問 Kuan 的事

你開的每個 subagent，prompt 裡都要把這一節照抄進去，並加上兩句：
- 「碰到任何一條，停下來，把草稿或要做的事回傳給 PM，不要自己執行。」
- 「如果你要再開 subagent，也要把這一節照抄進去。」

1. **任何對外訊息**，包括 Slack、email、GitHub issue、PR、comment。
   - 先把全文貼給她，她說 ok 才送。
   - Slack 草稿用中文，寫成一段可以直接複製的文字，格式見記憶 `project_cohort_issue_workflow`。
   - `#ai-fellows-program`（C0C4256NQ10）是 Slack Connect 頻道，Slack MCP 只能建草稿（`slack_send_message_draft`），由她自己按送出。
   - 跟 Wei 的 DM 也要先給她看稿。
2. **任何寫到 GitHub 的動作。** Kuan 在 curriculum、work-sim-alpha、catalyte-ai-skills 都有 push 權限，所以不能只靠權限擋。這裡用「白名單」：只有下面列出的可以用，其他一律先問。
   - **git：** 只能用以下指令：
     - 讀取類：clone、fetch、pull、log、diff、show、status、ls-remote、rev-parse、archive、submodule、`remote -v`、`remote get-url`、`config --get`
     - 本機變更類：branch、checkout、switch、add、commit
     - 保護設定：config、remote set-url，只用在下面的保險設定

     `git push` 在任何形式下都禁止，包括寫明網址的 push、加 `--no-verify` 的 push，以及 `--dry-run`。
   - **加 remote：** 不准新增 remote。pushurl 只擋得住 origin。
   - **gh：** 只能用 `view`、`list`、`status`、`auth status`、`repo clone`。`gh api` 只能做 GET，不准加 `-X`、`-f`、`-F`、`--input`。
   - **GitHub MCP：** 只能用名稱開頭是 `get_`、`list_`、`search_` 的工具。
   - **技術上的保險：** 每個 clone 下來的 repo 都執行下面幾行：
     ```
     git -C <repo> remote set-url --push origin no-push://disabled
     printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "push disabled by PM handoff" >&2\nexit 1\n' > <repo>/.git/hooks/pre-push
     chmod +x <repo>/.git/hooks/pre-push
     ```
   - **之後拿到 submodule 時**（submodule 裡的 `.git` 是檔案不是資料夾，要用下面這個寫法）：
     ```
     git submodule foreach 'git remote set-url --push origin no-push://disabled; h=$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks)/pre-push; printf "#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n" > "$h"; chmod +x "$h"'
     ```
3. **寫入任何共用系統**，包括 Classroom、Notion 的課程頁、Drive、Work Sim 網站、GitRoll 的任何服務。
   - 本機跑 pipeline 時，五個服務一律設成 `not-used`，或用 Kuan 核准過的沙盒。
   - 設定檔是各 challenge 的 `trainer/delivery/project-config.yaml`，範本在 `templates/challenge/project-config.yaml`。第一次跑之前，先把設定檔給她看。
   - curriculum 的 `.claude/skills/classroom-delivery` 等 skill 會寫入 Classroom，不要觸發。
   - 唯一的例外是她的私人 Notion 頁，見階段 1。
4. **跑 pipeline 的任何部分**，包括下面三種：
   - `start-challenge-generation` 的 paper round。它會依 `references/credentials.md` 去探測服務，其中 Classroom 的探測會「建立再刪除一份草稿」，屬於寫入。
   - `curriculum-challenge-design`、`run-assessment-scans`、`test-curriculum-challenge`、`calibrate-curriculum-challenge`。
   - 本機的訪談測試和評分測試。

   每次跑之前都要先報：要跑什麼、會碰到哪些服務、預估的 token 和時間，等她同意。參考數字：E 那一輪約一天、1.387 億 token，用的是 Wei 的帳號；在 Kuan 這邊跑，用的是她的帳號。
5. **安裝 plugin、改全域設定、拉大型 Docker image。** 例如安裝 `catalyte-ai-skills` plugin，這個目前沒裝，所以 `/catalyte-ai-skills:prep-goal` 現在叫不出來。
6. **花錢的事**，例如 GCP、任何付費 API、需要金鑰的模型呼叫。
   - Work Sim 的受訪者用的是 Google Vertex 上的 Gemini。
   - 她名下 GCP 專案的帳單是公司的真帳戶。
7. **刪除或覆蓋她的檔案。** 覆蓋前先 `cp FILE FILE.bak-YYYYMMDD`。
8. **絕不在下面這三個本機資料夾裡開 session 或 subagent**，也就是不能把它們當 cwd，也不在裡面跑任何 git 指令：
   - `~/Code/financial-health-brief`（Project A）
   - `~/Code/regulatory-compliance`（Project B）
   - `~/Code/event-coordination`（Project C 的 fork，名字跟 curriculum 裡的 C 資料夾一樣，不要搞混）

   - **原因：** 這三個資料夾都裝了 entire.io 的錄製 hook（2026-10-11 用 `find ~/Code ~/Documents -maxdepth 3 -name .entire` 查過，只有這三個）。在裡面開的 session 或跑的 git 指令，都可能被錄進她自己的 passport。錄製設定在三個地方：
     - `.entire/` 資料夾
     - `.claude/settings.json` 裡的 session hook
     - `.git/hooks/` 裡的 pre-push、post-commit、commit-msg、prepare-commit-msg、post-rewrite

     A 另外還有 `.claude/auto-commit.sh`，會自動 commit。
   - **要讀：** 只能從外面用絕對路徑讀檔案。任何 git 指令都不跑，連 `status` 也不行，因為 `status` 會改寫 `.git/index`。也不要改它們的任何設定。
   - **要複製一份來用（例如拿來測評分）：** 不要從本機資料夾複製，原因有兩個：`cp -r` 會連 hook 一起複製，本機記錄的版本也可能是舊的。改成從 GitHub 用一般的 `git clone` 另外抓一份乾淨的副本。
     - 不要用 `gh repo clone`。這三個 repo 都是 GitRollTraining repo 的 fork，`gh repo clone` 會自動多加一個指向上游的 `upstream` remote，而 pushurl 的保險只擋得住 origin。
     - clone 完立刻刪掉錄製設定，再加上規則 2 的保險：
     ```
     D=~/Documents/challenge-pipeline/submissions/<repo>
     git clone https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git "$D"
     rm -rf "$D/.claude" "$D/.entire"
     git -C "$D" remote set-url --push origin no-push://disabled
     printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "push disabled by PM handoff" >&2\nexit 1\n' > "$D/.git/hooks/pre-push"
     chmod +x "$D/.git/hooks/pre-push"
     git -C "$D" remote -v
     ```
     最後一行應該只列出 origin。新 clone 的副本不會帶到本機的 git hook，但 `.claude` 和 `.entire` 是 repo 裡追蹤的檔案，所以要手動刪掉。
   - **用哪個版本：** A 和 B 正式交件、被 Engine 評分的，是哪個 GitHub repo 的哪個 commit，要在階段 2 之前一起問 Kuan。可能的位置：
     - A：`kuanrur/financial-health-brief`，或它在 GitRollTraining 的上游
     - B：`kuanrur/regulatory-compliance`，或 `GitRollTraining/regulatory-compliance`

     版本搞錯的話，拿去跟正式分數比對就沒有意義。
   - **記憶要以這份交接檔為準：** 記憶 `project_catalyte_fellowship` 裡有兩句舊資訊，一是「只有 A 裝了 hook」，二是「用 `git archive` 複製」。兩句都以這裡為準，記憶檔也已經在 2026-10-11 更正。
9. **GitRoll 私有 repo 的內容，不放進 Artifact 或任何公開的地方。**

如果你要再開 subagent，也要把這一節照抄進去。

# Claude in Chrome

Claude in Chrome is a browser extension. Its tools, named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`, act in the person's real Chrome, in new tabs alongside the person's own, with their existing sign-ins. Claude in Chrome is available only while the person's Chrome is running with the extension connected; if its tool calls report that the extension is not connected or get no response, Claude says so rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

If the only Claude in Chrome tool present is `enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome`, Claude calls it first: it turns Claude in Chrome on for this conversation, and the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools appear once it has run.

## Loading the tools

If the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools are deferred (meaning they have to be loaded through ToolSearch before use), Claude loads every tool it expects to need in ONE ToolSearch call, because the select query accepts a comma-separated list and each extra ToolSearch call costs a full round trip. The core set to start with:

```
ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"
```

Claude adds task-specific tools to that same call when the task obviously needs them: `read_console_messages` and `read_network_requests` for debugging, `form_input` for forms, `gif_creator` for recordings, `javascript_tool` for page scripting. A second ToolSearch is only for a tool the task turned out to need later.

## Starting a session: tab context first, then a new tab

At the start of each browser session Claude calls `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp` first, to see the person's current tabs and understand what they may want to work with. Then:

1. Claude reuses an existing tab only when the person explicitly asks to work with it.
2. Otherwise Claude opens a new tab with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp` and works there, and, unless the person wants them kept, closes the tabs it created before finishing.
3. Claude never reuses tab IDs remembered from an earlier or different session. If a tool reports that a tab does not exist or is invalid, or the person closes a tab, or a navigation error occurs, Claude calls `tabs_context_mcp` again for fresh tab IDs.

## Site permissions

Claude in Chrome acts on a site only once the person has allowed it; depending on their settings the person may be prompted per site, in the extension or in the app. When a tool call is waiting on or refused that permission, Claude tells the person and waits for them to allow it rather than working around it. A site the person declines is their decision; Claude moves on.

## Recording a GIF

For multi-step interactions the person may want to review or share, Claude can record them with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator`. Claude captures a few extra frames before and after each action so playback is smooth, and gives the file a meaningful name (for example "login_process.gif").

## Reading console output

`mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages` reads the page's console. Console output can be verbose, so when Claude is looking for specific entries it passes the `pattern` parameter (a regular expression), for example pattern "[MyApp]" to keep only the application's own logs.

## Alerts and dialogs

Claude does not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or other browser modal dialogs through its actions. Those dialogs block all further browser events, so the extension stops receiving commands. Instead:

1. Claude avoids clicking elements likely to raise a confirmation dialog (for example a "Delete" button) unless necessary.
2. If it must interact with such an element, Claude warns the person first that this may interrupt the session.
3. Claude can use `mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool` to check for and dismiss an existing dialog before proceeding, and prefers `console.log` plus `read_console_messages` over `alert` for debugging.

If a dialog does get triggered and the browser stops responding, Claude tells the person they need to dismiss it manually in Chrome.

## Staying on task, and when to stop

Claude stays focused on the specific task and does not wander into unrelated pages. Claude stops and asks the person how to proceed, explaining what it tried and what went wrong, when any of these happen:

- browser tool calls fail or return errors after 2 or 3 attempts
- the extension gives no response
- page elements do not respond to clicks or input, or pages do not load or time out
- the task turns out to involve unexpected complexity or tangents
- several approaches have not completed the task

Claude does not keep retrying the same failing action.

# Classification guide excerpt

Linden Shore Mutual, workers' compensation, Maryland. Edition of July 2025. Internal use by underwriting and premium
audit.

This excerpt holds the general paragraphs and the class codes our current new-business employers fall under. Audit
files cite a paragraph by its identifier (CG-01, CG-02 and so on). A class code is cited by the paragraph that
describes it.

## General

**CG-01. Premium basis.** Premium is charged per USD 100 of payroll in each class code at the rate underwriting sets
for that code. Payroll is reported for the policy period being audited.

**CG-02. Assigning codes.** An employer is assigned the class code that describes its principal business. An employee
whose work is described by another code in this guide is reported under that code. An employer may carry several codes.

**CG-03. Payroll.** Payroll is the gross remuneration paid to employees for the period: wages, salaries, commissions
and bonuses. Expense reimbursements that the employer can document, such as travel and lodging costs, are not payroll.

**CG-05. Owners and executive officers.** An owner or executive officer who has filed an election of exclusion is not
counted. An owner who is included is counted under the code for the work the owner does.

**CG-06. Subcontractors.** Payments to a subcontractor who does not carry workers' compensation insurance for its own
workers may be treated as payroll of the employer, under the code for the work the subcontractor performed.

**CG-07. Division of payroll.** When an employee performs work in more than one classification and the employer keeps
records of the time spent in each, the employee's payroll may be divided between the codes.

## Class codes

**CG-04. C-110 Clerical office employees.** Employees whose duties are confined to an office: correspondence,
bookkeeping, dispatching by telephone or radio, drafting and estimating at a desk, and professional staff who work in
the office.

**CG-11. R-310 Roofing.** Installation, repair and removal of roofs and roof coverings on any building, including
work on scaffolds and ladders at the roof line.

**CG-12. R-320 Siding and gutters.** Installation and repair of exterior siding, gutters, downspouts and exterior trim
below the roof line. Roofing work is described by CG-11.

**CG-13. L-620 Landscaping and lawn care.** Lawn mowing, planting, mulching and the care of grounds.

**CG-15. H-420 Residential homebuilding.** Construction and remodeling of dwellings: framing, drywall, interior
finish, carpentry and general labor at the building site. Roofing work is described by CG-11 and electrical wiring
by CG-21.

**CG-21. E-510 Electrical wiring.** Installation and repair of electrical wiring and fixtures inside buildings,
including service connections.

**CG-22. M-830 Metal fabrication shop.** Cutting, bending and welding of sheet and structural metal in a shop.

**CG-31. T-610 Courier and delivery drivers.** Drivers of vans and light trucks delivering parcels and documents,
and helpers who ride on the delivery vehicles.

**CG-35. G-950 Parking garage attendants.** Parking and retrieving customer vehicles.

**CG-41. F-710 Restaurants.** Preparation and service of meals: kitchen staff, servers, hosts and dishwashers.

**CG-42. F-720 Off-site caterers.** Preparation of food and its service at events away from the employer's premises,
including the catering crew of an employer that also runs a restaurant.

**CG-51. N-910 Home health care.** Personal care and nursing services in clients' homes.

"""Write the per-employer CSV and the employer's sections of the audit report and questions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import re
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

from allocate import ZERO, Result

CSV_HEADER = ["class_code", "payroll_allocated", "rationale_ref"]

REPORT_TITLE = """# Audit report: class codes and payroll allocation

First-pass classification by the class-code-assistant Skill. Amounts are US dollars for each employer's audit period.
The Skill classifies and allocates payroll only; it does not set rates or quote premium. Each section says whether the
employer's own split is accepted, every adjustment with its amount, and the records that decided it. Paragraph
identifiers (CG-nn) are cited from the classification guide read during the run.
"""

QUESTIONS_TITLE = """# Audit questions for the employers

Questions for the premium auditor to put to each employer before signing off. Each one names the employee,
subcontractor or record it is about. Every adjustment and every record the allocation relies on is covered by at least
one question.
"""


def codes_csv(result: Result) -> str:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(CSV_HEADER)
    for code, amount, ref in result.lines():
        w.writerow([code, f"{amount:.2f}", ref])
    return buf.getvalue()


def _md(text: str) -> str:
    return text.replace("|", "\\|")


def _decision(r: Result) -> str:
    reg = r.employer.record_files["payroll_register"]
    if r.accepted:
        others = [f for f in r.records_used if f not in (reg, "field-notes.md")]
        checked = f", checked against {', '.join(others)}" if others else ""
        return (f"**Decision: the employer's own split is accepted.** The payroll register ({reg}) gives the same codes and "
                f"amounts to the cent{checked}, and no record shows payroll that can be measured under another code.")
    files = []
    for a in r.adjustments:
        for f in a.records:
            if f not in files:
                files.append(f)
    return (f"**Decision: the employer's own split is not accepted.** The employer's records disagree with the application, "
            f"and the records decide. The allocation rests on {', '.join(files)}.")


def report_section(r: Result) -> str:
    e = r.employer
    out = [f"## {e.name}", ""]
    files = ["application.md", "business-description.md"]
    if e.field_notes:
        files.append("field-notes.md")
    files += [f for f in e.record_files.values()]
    out.append(f"Application {e.application_id}. Audit period {e.period_start} to {e.period_end}. Classification guide "
               f"edition {r.guide.edition}. Employer file read: {', '.join(files)}.")
    if e.unused_files:
        out.append("Not used for the allocation: " + "; ".join(f"{k} ({v})" for k, v in e.unused_files.items()) + ".")
    out += ["", _decision(r), "", "### Codes and payroll allocated", "",
            "| Class code | Payroll allocated | Rationale ref | Code described as |", "|---|---:|---|---|"]
    total = ZERO
    for code, amount, ref in r.lines():
        out.append(f"| {code} | {amount:.2f} | {ref} | {r.guide.code_paragraph(code).code_name} |")
        total += amount
    out += [f"| Total | {total:.2f} | | |", "", f"Principal business code: {r.governing_code}; {r.governing_basis}.", ""]

    out += ["### Compared with the employer's own split", "",
            "| Class code | Employer reported | Allocated | Difference |", "|---|---:|---:|---:|"]
    reported, alloc = r.reported, r.by_code
    rep_total = ZERO
    for code in [c for c in r.guide.codes if c in reported or c in alloc]:
        rv, av = reported.get(code, ZERO), alloc.get(code, ZERO)
        rep_total += rv
        out.append(f"| {code} | {rv:.2f} | {av:.2f} | {av - rv:+.2f} |")
    out += [f"| Total | {rep_total:.2f} | {total:.2f} | {total - rep_total:+.2f} |", ""]
    if e.employer_note:
        out += [f"Employer's note on the application: \"{e.employer_note}\"", ""]
    if r.employer_assignment:
        names = {s.key: s.label for s in r.subjects}
        per_code: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for eid, code in r.employer_assignment.items():
            per_code.setdefault(code, []).append(names[eid])
        out.append("The employer's figures match these employees on the register: "
                   + "; ".join(f"{c}: {', '.join(n)}" for c, n in per_code.items()) + ".")
        out.append("")
    if not r.accepted:
        out.append("Where and why the allocation differs:")
        out.append("")
        for code in [c for c in r.guide.codes if c in reported or c in alloc]:
            diff = alloc.get(code, ZERO) - reported.get(code, ZERO)
            if diff:
                ins = [a for a in r.adjustments if a.to_code == code]
                outs = [a for a in r.adjustments if a.from_code == code]
                parts = []
                if ins:
                    parts.append("in: " + "; ".join(f"{a.subject} {a.amount:.2f}" for a in ins))
                if outs:
                    parts.append("out: " + "; ".join(f"{a.subject} {a.amount:.2f}" for a in outs))
                out.append(f"- {code} {diff:+.2f} ({' | '.join(parts)})")
        out.append("")

    out += ["### Adjustments", ""]
    if r.adjustments:
        out += ["| # | Employee or payment | Amount | From | To | Why | Records | Guide |", "|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for i, a in enumerate(r.adjustments, 1):
            out.append(f"| {i} | {_md(a.subject)} | {a.amount:.2f} | {a.from_code or 'not reported'} | {a.to_code or 'not counted'} | "
                       f"{_md(a.reason)} | {', '.join(a.records)} | {', '.join(a.refs)} |")
    else:
        out.append("None. Every employee's payroll stays under the code the employer reported.")
    out.append("")
    if r.excluded:
        out += ["### Paid but not counted as payroll", "", "| Employee or payment | Amount | Why |", "|---|---:|---|"]
        for who, amount, why in r.excluded:
            out.append(f"| {_md(who)} | {amount:.2f} | {_md(why)} |")
        out.append("")

    out += ["### Allocation by employee and payment", "", "| Employee or payment | Class code | Amount | Basis | Records |", "|---|---|---:|---|---|"]
    for s in r.subjects:
        for p in s.portions:
            out.append(f"| {_md(s.label)} | {p.code} | {p.amount:.2f} | {_md(p.basis)} | {', '.join(p.records)} |")
    out += ["", "### Records that decided this file", ""]
    for f, what in r.records_used.items():
        out.append(f"- {f}: {what}.")
    out.append("")
    if r.assumptions:
        out += ["### Assumptions where the guide is silent", ""]
        out += [f"- {a}" for a in r.assumptions]
        out.append("")
    if r.notes:
        out += ["### Notes", ""]
        out += [f"- {n}" for n in r.notes]
        out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out).rstrip() + "\n"


def questions_section(r: Result) -> str:
    out = [f"## {r.employer.name}", ""]
    for i, q in enumerate(r.questions, 1):
        out.append(f"{i}. **{q.subject}.** {q.text}")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"<!-- BEGIN employer:(?P<slug>[a-z0-9-]+) -->\n(?P<body>.*?)<!-- END employer:(?P=slug) -->\n", re.S)


def merge_sections(path: Path, title: str, slug: str, body: str, order: list[str]) -> None:
    """Insert or replace one employer's section; keep sections in the configured order."""
    sections: dict[str, str] = {}
    if path.exists():
        for m in SECTION_RE.finditer(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
            sections[m.group("slug")] = m.group("body")
    sections[slug] = body
    ranked = sorted(sections, key=lambda s: (order.index(s) if s in order else len(order), s))
    parts = [title]
    for s in ranked:
        parts.append(f"<!-- BEGIN employer:{s} -->\n{sections[s]}<!-- END employer:{s} -->\n")
    path.write_text("\n".join(parts), encoding="utf-8")


def run_record(r: Result, sources: dict) -> dict:
    def d(x: Decimal) -> str:
        return f"{x:.2f}"

    return {
        "employer": r.employer.slug,
        "name": r.employer.name,
        "application": r.employer.application_id,
        "audit_period": [str(r.employer.period_start), str(r.employer.period_end)],
        "guide_edition": r.guide.edition,
        "sources": sources,
        "accepted_employer_split": r.accepted,
        "reported": {c: d(v) for c, v in r.reported.items()},
        "allocated": [{"class_code": c, "payroll_allocated": d(a), "rationale_ref": ref} for c, a, ref in r.lines()],
        "principal_business_code": r.governing_code,
        "subjects": [
            {"label": s.label, "kind": s.kind, "employer_code": s.employer_code,
             "portions": [{"code": p.code, "amount": d(p.amount), "basis": p.basis, "records": p.records, "refs": p.refs} for p in s.portions]}
            for s in r.subjects
        ],
        "excluded": [{"label": w, "amount": d(a), "why": y} for w, a, y in r.excluded],
        "adjustments": [{"subject": a.subject, "amount": d(a.amount), "from": a.from_code, "to": a.to_code, "reason": a.reason, "records": a.records, "refs": a.refs} for a in r.adjustments],
        "questions": [{"subject": q.subject, "text": q.text} for q in r.questions],
        "assumptions": r.assumptions,
        "records_used": r.records_used,
    }

"""Run the class-code assistant on one or more employer files.

Reads the classification guide and the employer files from the audit team's Drive
folder at the start of every run (or from a local copy given with --source-dir),
then writes, per employer:

    deliverables/codes/<employer>.csv
    deliverables/audit-report.md      (the employer's section)
    deliverables/audit-questions.md   (the employer's section)
    runs/<employer>.json              (run record: sources read, allocation, questions)

Examples:
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --employer harbor-point-legal
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --all
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --employer-dir ~/Downloads/new-employer
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SKILL_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REPO = SKILL_DIR.parent.parent

from allocate import allocate  # noqa: E402
from employer import EmployerFileError, load_employer  # noqa: E402
from fetch_drive import FetchError, fetch_folder  # noqa: E402
from guide import GuideError, load_guide  # noqa: E402
from render import QUESTIONS_TITLE, REPORT_TITLE, codes_csv, merge_sections, questions_section, report_section, run_record  # noqa: E402


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Suggest class codes, allocate payroll and draft audit questions.")
    pick = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    pick.add_argument("--employer", action="append", metavar="SLUG", help="employer folder name, for example harbor-point-legal (repeatable)")
    pick.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", help="every employer folder in the source")
    pick.add_argument("--employer-dir", type=Path, help="a local employer folder that is not in the Drive folder")
    ap.add_argument("--source-dir", type=Path, help="use a local copy of the audit folder instead of reading Drive")
    ap.add_argument("--cache-dir", type=Path, default=REPO / ".cache" / "drive", help="where the Drive folder is downloaded")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=REPO, help="repository root to write deliverables/ and runs/ into")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    config = json.loads((SKILL_DIR / "sources.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    sources = {"guide_file": config["guide_file"], "employers_folder": config["employers_folder"]}
    try:
        if args.source_dir:
            root = args.source_dir.expanduser().resolve()
            sources["read_from"] = f"local copy {root}"
        else:
            root = args.cache_dir.resolve()
            if root.exists():
                shutil.rmtree(root)
            fetch_folder(config["drive_folder_id"], root)
            sources["read_from"] = f"Google Drive folder '{config['drive_folder_name']}' ({config['drive_folder_id']})"
        sources["read_at_utc"] = dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
        guide_path = root / config["guide_file"]
        if not guide_path.exists():
            raise GuideError(f"classification guide {config['guide_file']} not found in {root}")
        guide = load_guide(guide_path)
    except (FetchError, GuideError) as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    employers_root = root / config["employers_folder"]
    if args.employer_dir:
        folders = [args.employer_dir.expanduser().resolve()]
    else:
        available = sorted(p.name for p in employers_root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()) if employers_root.is_dir() else []
        wanted = available if args.all else args.employer
        missing = [s for s in wanted if s not in available]
        if missing:
            print(f"error: no employer folder named {', '.join(missing)}; available: {', '.join(available) or 'none'}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        folders = [employers_root / s for s in wanted]

    out = args.out.resolve()
    (out / "deliverables" / "codes").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (out / "runs").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    order = config.get("report_order", [])
    failed = 0
    for folder in folders:
        try:
            emp = load_employer(folder)
            result = allocate(emp, guide)
        except (EmployerFileError, GuideError, ValueError) as exc:
            failed += 1
            print(f"error: {folder.name}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        (out / "deliverables" / "codes" / f"{emp.slug}.csv").write_text(codes_csv(result), encoding="utf-8")
        merge_sections(out / "deliverables" / "audit-report.md", REPORT_TITLE, emp.slug, report_section(result), order)
        merge_sections(out / "deliverables" / "audit-questions.md", QUESTIONS_TITLE, emp.slug, questions_section(result), order)
        files = {p.name: sha256(p) for p in sorted(folder.iterdir()) if p.is_file()}
        record = run_record(result, {**sources, "guide_sha256": sha256(guide_path), "employer_files_sha256": files})
        (out / "runs" / f"{emp.slug}.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        verdict = "accepted" if result.accepted else "not accepted"
        codes = ", ".join(f"{c} {a:.2f}" for c, a, _ in result.lines())
        print(f"{emp.slug}: employer split {verdict}; {codes}; {len(result.adjustments)} adjustments, {len(result.questions)} questions")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Check the Skill's outputs against the assignment's format rules and the source records.

Run after run_audit.py. It re-reads the guide and the payroll registers from the same
source the run used (the Drive cache by default) and checks, for every employer:

- deliverables/codes/<employer>.csv exists, has exactly the header
  class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref, one row per code, no zero rows,
  dollars to the cent without separators, and a rationale_ref that is the guide
  paragraph describing that code;
- the CSV total equals the payroll register total plus the additions the run reports
  (uninsured subcontractors, undocumented allowances), and every employee's portions
  add up to the register wages;
- audit-report.md and audit-questions.md have one section per employer; the report
  shows every code, amount and adjustment; every adjustment and every record relied on
  is named in at least one question, and every question names its subject.

Exit status 0 when every check passes, 1 otherwise.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import re
import sys
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

SKILL_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REPO = SKILL_DIR.parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from guide import load_guide  # noqa: E402
from render import SECTION_RE  # noqa: E402

AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d{2}$")


def sections(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {m.group("slug"): m.group("body") for m in SECTION_RE.finditer(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--source-dir", type=Path, default=REPO / ".cache" / "drive")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=REPO)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    config = json.loads((SKILL_DIR / "sources.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    src, out = args.source_dir.resolve(), args.out.resolve()
    guide = load_guide(src / config["guide_file"])
    failures: list[str] = []
    checks = 0

    def check(ok: bool, message: str) -> None:
        nonlocal checks
        checks += 1
        if not ok:
            failures.append(message)

    runs = sorted((out / "runs").glob("*.json"))
    check(bool(runs), "no run records in runs/; run run_audit.py first")
    slugs = [r.stem for r in runs]
    for expected in config.get("report_order", []):
        check(expected in slugs, f"no run for {expected}")
    report = sections(out / "deliverables" / "audit-report.md")
    questions = sections(out / "deliverables" / "audit-questions.md")

    for run_path in runs:
        run = json.loads(run_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        slug = run["employer"]
        where = slug

        # CSV format.
        csv_path = out / "deliverables" / "codes" / f"{slug}.csv"
        check(csv_path.exists(), f"{where}: {csv_path.name} missing")
        if not csv_path.exists():
            continue
        raw = csv_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        check(raw.splitlines()[0] == "class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref", f"{where}: CSV header is not exact")
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(raw.splitlines()))
        codes_seen = set()
        csv_total = Decimal("0")
        for row in rows:
            code, amount, ref = row["class_code"], row["payroll_allocated"], row["rationale_ref"]
            check(code not in codes_seen, f"{where}: {code} appears twice")
            codes_seen.add(code)
            check(guide.has_code(code), f"{where}: {code} is not in the guide")
            check(bool(AMOUNT_RE.match(amount)), f"{where}: {code} amount {amount!r} is not dollars to the cent without separators")
            check(Decimal(amount) > 0, f"{where}: {code} has zero payroll")
            if guide.has_code(code):
                check(ref == guide.code_paragraph(code).id, f"{where}: {code} cites {ref}, the guide describes it in {guide.code_paragraph(code).id}")
            check(ref in guide.paragraphs, f"{where}: rationale_ref {ref} is not a paragraph of the guide")
            csv_total += Decimal(amount)

        # Totals against the payroll register read again from the source.
        reg_name = next((f for f, what in run["records_used"].items() if what.startswith("gross wages")), "payroll-register.csv")
        reg_rows = list(csv.DictReader((src / config["employers_folder"] / slug / reg_name).open(encoding="utf-8")))
        reg_total = sum(Decimal(r["wages_paid"]) for r in reg_rows)
        additions = sum(Decimal(a["amount"]) for a in run["adjustments"] if a["from"] is None and a["to"])
        removed = sum(Decimal(a["amount"]) for a in run["adjustments"] if a["to"] is None)
        owners_out = sum(Decimal(e["amount"]) for e in run["excluded"] if "election of exclusion" in e["why"])
        check(csv_total == reg_total + additions - removed - owners_out,
              f"{where}: CSV total {csv_total} != register {reg_total} + additions {additions} - removed {removed + owners_out}")
        wages = {f"{r['name']} ({r['employee_id']})": Decimal(r["wages_paid"]) for r in reg_rows}
        for s in run["subjects"]:
            if s["kind"] != "employee":
                continue
            base = sum(Decimal(p["amount"]) for p in s["portions"] if "allowance not backed" not in p["basis"])
            check(base == wages.get(s["label"]), f"{where}: {s['label']} portions {base} != register wages {wages.get(s['label'])}")
        check(len([s for s in run["subjects"] if s["kind"] == "employee"]) + sum(1 for e in run["excluded"] if "election of exclusion" in e["why"]) == len(reg_rows),
              f"{where}: not every employee on the register was allocated")

        # Report section.
        body = report.get(slug, "")
        check(bool(body), f"{where}: no section in audit-report.md")
        check(f"## {run['name']}" in body, f"{where}: report section heading is not the employer name")
        for row in rows:
            check(f"| {row['class_code']} | {row['payroll_allocated']} | {row['rationale_ref']} |" in body, f"{where}: report does not show {row['class_code']} {row['payroll_allocated']}")
        decision = "accepted.**" if run["accepted_employer_split"] else "not accepted.**"
        check(decision in body, f"{where}: report decision does not match the run")
        for a in run["adjustments"]:
            check(a["amount"] in body and a["subject"] in body, f"{where}: report misses adjustment {a['subject']} {a['amount']}")
        for f in run["records_used"]:
            check(f in body, f"{where}: report does not name record {f}")

        # Questions section.
        qbody = questions.get(slug, "")
        check(bool(qbody), f"{where}: no section in audit-questions.md")
        items = re.findall(r"^\d+\. \*\*(.+?)\.\*\* (.+)$", qbody, re.M)
        check(len(items) == len(run["questions"]), f"{where}: question count differs from the run")
        names = [s["label"].split(" (")[0] for s in run["subjects"]] + [s["label"].split(",")[0] for s in run["subjects"]]
        files = list(run["records_used"])
        for subject, text in items:
            check(any(n in subject for n in names) or any(f in subject for f in files) or re.search(r"[A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z][a-z]+", subject) is not None,
                  f"{where}: question subject '{subject}' does not name an employee, subcontractor or record")
        for a in run["adjustments"]:
            who = a["subject"].split(" (")[0].split(",")[0]
            check(any(who in s or who in t for s, t in items), f"{where}: no question covers adjustment for {a['subject']}")
        for f in files:
            if f == "field-notes.md":
                continue
            check(any(f in s or f in t for s, t in items), f"{where}: no question asks the employer to confirm {f}")

    check(not (out / "interviews").exists() or not any((out / "interviews").iterdir()), "interviews/ has files; this test conducted no interview")
    for f in failures:
        print(f"FAIL {f}")
    print(f"{checks - len(failures)} of {checks} checks passed for {len(runs)} employers")
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
